<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>{{Verse|3|3}} But thou, O {{sc|Lord}}, {{smaller|art}} a ſheild ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, about''}} for me; my glory, and the lifter vp of mine head.

{{Verse|3|4}} I cryed vnto the {{sc|Lord}} with my voyce, and he heard me out of holy hill. Selah.

{{Verse|3|5}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.4.9}} I layd me downe and ſlept: I awaked, for the {{sc|Lord}} ſuſtained me.

{{Verse|3|6}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.27.3}} I will not be afraid of ten thouſands of people, that haue ſet {{smaller|themſelues}} againſt me round about.

{{Verse|3|7}} Ariſe, O {{sc|Lord}}, ſaue mee, O my God; for thou haſt ſmitten all mine enemies {{smaller|vpon}} the cheeke bone: thou haſt broken the teeth of the vngodly.

{{Verse|3|8}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iſa. 43.11. Hoſ.I3.4.}} Saluation {{smaller|belongeth}} vnto the {{LORD}}, thy bleſſing {{smaller|is}} vpon thy people. Selah.

==={{Chapter|4|PSAL. IIII.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#4:1|1]] Dauid prayeth for audience. [[#4:2|2]] He reproueth and exhorteth this enemies. [[#4:6|6]] Mans happineſſe is in Gods fauour.}}

¶ To The ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, ouerſeer''.}} chiefe Muſician on Neginoth, A Pſalme of David.

{{Verse|4|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|H|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (H).png|imgsize=100px}}Eare me, when I call, O God of my righteouſneſſe: thou haſt inlarged mee when {{smaller|I was}} in diſtreſſe, ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, bee gracious vnto me.''}} haue mercy vpon me, and heare my prayer.

{{Verse|4|2}}  O ye ſonnes of men, how long {{smaller|will yee turne}} my glory into ſhame? {{smaller|how long}} will yee loue vanitie, {{smaller|and}} ſeeke after leaſing? Selah.

{{Verse|4|3}} But know that {{sc|Lord}} hath ſet apart him that is godly, for himſelfe: the {{sc|Lord}} will heare when I call vnto him.

{{Verse|4|4}} Stand in awe, and ſinne not: commune with your owne heart vpon your bed, and be ſtill. Selah.

{{Verse|4|5}} Offer *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.50.14.& 51.19}} the ſacrifices of righteouſneſſe, and put your truſt in the {{sc|Lord}}.

{{Verse|4|6}} There be many that ſay, Who wil ſhew vs {{smaller|any}} good? {{sc|Lord}} lift thou vp the light of thy countenance vpon us.

{{Verse|4|7}} Thou haſt put gladneſſe in my heart, more then in the time {{smaller|that}} their corne and their wine increaſed.

{{Verse|4|8}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.3.5}} I will both lay mee downe in peace, and ſleepe: for thou {{sc|Lord}} only makeſt me dwell in ſafetie.

==={{Chapter|5|PSAL. V.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#5:1|1]] Dauid prayeth, and profeſſeth his ſtudie in prayer. [[#5:4|4]] God fauoureth not the wicked. [[#5:7|7]] David profeſsing his faith, prayeth vnto God, to guide him, [[#5:10|10]] To deſtroy his enemies, [[#5:11|11]] and to preſerue the godly.}}

¶ To the chiefe muſician vpon Nehiloth, A Pſalme of Dauid

{{Verse|5|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|G|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (G).png|imgsize=100px}}Iue eare to my words, O {{sc|Lord}}, conſider my meditation.

{{Verse|5|2}} Hearken vnto the voice of my crie, my King, and my God: for vnto thee will I pray.

{{Verse|5|3}} {{*}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.130.6}} My voyce ſhalt thou heare in the morning, O {{sc|Lord}}; in the morning will I direct {{smaller|my prayer}} vnto thee, and will looke {{smaller|vp}}.

{{Verse|5|4}} For thou {{smaller|art}} not a God {{smaller|that}} hath pleaſure in wickedneſſe: neither ſhall euil dwell with thee.

{{Verse|5|5}} The foolish ſhall not ſtand †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. before thine eyes.''}} in thy ſight: thou hateſt al workers of iniquity

{{Verse|5|6}} Thou ſhalt deſtroy them that ſpeake leaſing: the {{sc|Lord}} will abhorre the †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. the man of bloods and deceit.''}} bloodie and deceitfull man.

{{Verse|5|7}} But as for me, I will come {{smaller|into}} thy houſe in the multitude of thy mercy: {{smaller|and}} in thy feare will I worſhip toward †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. the temple of thy holineſſe.''}} thy holy temple.

{{Verse|5|8}} Lead me O {{sc|Lord}}, in thy righteouſneſſe, becauſe of †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. thoſe which obſerue me.''}} mine enemies; make thy way ſtraight before my face.

{{Verse|5|9}} For {{smaller|there is}} no ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ''Or, ſtedfaſtneſſe.''}} faithfulnes †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. in his mouth. i. in the mouth of any of them.''}} in their mouth, their inward part {{smaller|is}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. wickedneſſes.''}} very wickedneſſe: *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=*Rom.3.13}} their throat {{smaller|is}} an open ſepulchre, they flatter with their tongue.

{{Verse|5|10}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, make them guilty.''}} Deſtroy thou them, O God, let them fall ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, from their counſels.''}} by their owne counſels: caſt them out in the multitude of their tranſgreſſions, for they have rebelled againſt thee.

{{Verse|5|11}} But let all thoſe that put their truſt in thee, reioyce: let them euer ſhout for ioy, becauſe thou †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. thou couereſt over, or protecteſt them.''}} defendeſt them: let them alſo that loue thy name, be ioyfull in thee.

{{Verse|5|12}} For thou, {{sc|Lord}}, wilt bleſſe the righteous: with fauour wilt thou †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. crowne him,''}} compaſſe him as {{smaller|with}} a ſhield.

==={{Chapter|6|PSAL. VI.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#6:1|1]] Dauids complaint in his ſickneſſe.[[#6:8|8]] By faith he triumpheth ouer his enemies.}}

¶ To the chiefe muſician on Neginoth ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, vpon the eight.''}} vpon Sheminith, A Pſalme of Dauid.

{{Verse|6|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|O|image=King James Bible (1611) page A4r (O).png|imgsize=100px}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſa.16.1}} {{sc|Lord}}, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chaſten me in thy hot diſpleaſure.

{{Verse|6|2}} Haue mercy vpon me, O {{sc|Lord}}, for I {{smaller|am}} weake: O {{sc|Lord}} heale mee, for my bones are vexed.
